changes.title: Declare that Contoso Integration depends on Contoso Core
changes.why: Contoso Integration uses Contoso Core (3 relations), but its app.json does not name Contoso Core. It compiles only as long as something else brings Contoso Core along.
how: Add Contoso Core to `dependencies` in the app.json of Contoso Integration: its id, name, publisher, and version.
Or, when Contoso Integration should not know Contoso Core: remove the use. The Apps lens shows the 3 relations between them.

changes.title: Bring in what Contoso Integration refers to
changes.why: Contoso Integration refers to objects (2 relations) that are in no app of this repository and in no symbol package. What depends on them, and what a change to them breaks, is not known.
how: Download the symbols of the apps it depends on into `.alpackages` (AL: Download Symbols), or add the app that holds them to the workspace.
Run BC Atlas again: the relations to these objects then show.

changes.title: CON Item Sync: declare the dependency; it points inward
changes.why: The codeunit CON Item Sync of Integration depends on table CON Item of Core, which the configured architecture does not allow.
how: Add Core to dependsOn of Integration in .bca.json (and to app.json when they are separate apps).
Or: go through a component you already depend on (effort M).

changes.title: Let Core own the writes to table 50000 CON Item
changes.why: The table 50000 CON Item belongs to Core, and Integration (codeunit 50201 CON Item Sync) writes it as well. Whoever changes the table has to know every one of them.
changes.brief: of Core, also written by Integration (codeunit 50201 CON Item Sync)
how: Put the writes behind a codeunit of Core and call it from Integration.
Or move the table to the component that writes it most, when it belongs there.

changes.title: Let Sales own the writes to table 50100 CON Sales Quote
changes.why: The table 50100 CON Sales Quote belongs to Sales, and Integration (codeunit 50200 CON Quote Export) writes it as well. Whoever changes the table has to know every one of them.
changes.brief: of Sales, also written by Integration (codeunit 50200 CON Quote Export)
how: Put the writes behind a codeunit of Sales and call it from Integration.
Or move the table to the component that writes it most, when it belongs there.

changes.title: Make 1 object of Core internal
changes.why: Nothing outside Core uses codeunit 50010 CON Standard Pricing. As long as it is public, other apps can start to depend on it, and every change is a breaking one.
how: `bca refactor surface --component "Core"` shows the change: Access = Internal on these objects, and what others use listed under `exposes` in .bca.json.

changes.title: Make 2 objects of Integration internal
changes.why: Nothing outside Integration uses codeunit 50200 CON Quote Export, codeunit 50201 CON Item Sync. As long as they are public, other apps can start to depend on them, and every change is a breaking one.
how: `bca refactor surface --component "Integration"` shows the change: Access = Internal on these objects, and what others use listed under `exposes` in .bca.json.

stories.title: What multi-app is
stories.summary: The system from the outside in: how it works, then its apps, components, hubs, data, events, the user interface, and its health.

steps.title: How it works
steps.text: From left to right: 2 screens, 6 logic objects, 3 tables. The screens run the logic, and the logic reads and writes the data. A line leads from what uses to what is used.

steps.title: multi-app
steps.text: 12 objects in 3 apps: 5 codeunits, 3 tables, 2 pages, 1 interface, 1 permissionset. Every dot is one of them, every line something one does with another. All of it is read from the AL source.

steps.title: The apps
steps.text: Contoso Core, Contoso Integration, Contoso Sales. A line is what one app uses of another.

steps.title: 3 components
steps.text: Core, Sales, Integration. Lower layers know nothing of higher ones.

steps.title: Core
steps.text: 6 objects: CON Item, CON Price Group, CON Item Card, CON Price Calculation, CON Standard Pricing, and 1 more.

steps.title: Sales
steps.text: 4 objects: CON Sales Quote, CON Quote Mgt., CON Sales Quote, CON Sales.

steps.title: Integration
steps.text: 2 objects: CON Quote Export, CON Item Sync. 1 dependency point the wrong way.

steps.title: What everything depends on
steps.text: CON Item (used by 4, uses 1); CON Sales Quote (used by 4, uses 1); CON Quote Mgt. (used by 3, uses 2); CON Standard Pricing (used by 1, uses 3); CON Quote Export (used by 0, uses 3). A change here reaches furthest.

steps.title: The data
steps.text: 3 tables: CON Item, CON Price Group, CON Sales Quote. Orange lines write, blue lines read.

steps.title: Events
steps.text: CON Quote Mgt., CON Pricing Mgt. publish events or subscribe to them. This is where other code can step in without changing these objects.

steps.title: Contracts
steps.text: 1 interface: CON Price Calculation. What implements an interface can be exchanged.

steps.title: The user interface
steps.text: 2 pages and reports: CON Item Card, CON Sales Quote.

steps.title: Permissions
steps.text: 1 permission set: CON Sales.

steps.title: Declare that Contoso Integration depends on Contoso Core
steps.text: Contoso Integration uses Contoso Core (3 relations), but its app.json does not name Contoso Core. It compiles only as long as something else brings Contoso Core along. How: Add Contoso Core to `dependencies` in the app.json of Contoso Integration: its id, name, publisher, and version. Or, when Contoso Integration should not know Contoso Core: remove the use. The Apps lens shows the 3 relations between them. Effort: S.

steps.title: Bring in what Contoso Integration refers to
steps.text: Contoso Integration refers to objects (2 relations) that are in no app of this repository and in no symbol package. What depends on them, and what a change to them breaks, is not known. How: Download the symbols of the apps it depends on into `.alpackages` (AL: Download Symbols), or add the app that holds them to the workspace. Run BC Atlas again: the relations to these objects then show. Effort: S.

steps.title: CON Item Sync: declare the dependency; it points inward

How: Add Core to dependsOn of Integration in .bca.json (and to app.json when they are separate apps). Or: go through a component you already depend on (effort M). Effort: S.

steps.title: Let Core own the writes to table 50000 CON Item
steps.text: The table 50000 CON Item belongs to Core, and Integration (codeunit 50201 CON Item Sync) writes it as well. Whoever changes the table has to know every one of them. How: Put the writes behind a codeunit of Core and call it from Integration. Or move the table to the component that writes it most, when it belongs there. Effort: M.

steps.text: The table 50100 CON Sales Quote belongs to Sales, and Integration (codeunit 50200 CON Quote Export) writes it as well. Whoever changes the table has to know every one of them. steps.title: Make 1 object of Core internal
steps.text: Nothing outside Core uses codeunit 50010 CON Standard Pricing. As long as it is public, other apps can start to depend on it, and every change is a breaking one. How: `bca refactor surface --component "Core"` shows the change: Access = Internal on these objects, and what others use listed under `exposes` in .bca.json. Add `--apply` to write it. Effort: S.
